'''Yekaterinburg TV Tower''' ({{langx|ru|Екатеринбу́ргская телеба́шня}}) was a tall incomplete structure in [[Yekaterinburg]], [[Russia]]. Construction work started 1983, but was put on hold in 1991, following the [[collapse of the Soviet Union]],<ref name="BBC">{{cite news|title=Massive incomplete TV tower demolished|work=BBC News |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/av/world-europe-43527063/massive-incomplete-tv-tower-in-russia-demolished|access-date=24 March 2018}} (includes video of the demolition)</ref> as its shaft reached the height of {{convert|220|m|feet|abbr=on}}.<ref name="web1">{{cite web|title=Yekaterinburg Television Tower|url=http://en.structurae.de/structures/data/index.cfm?ID=s0016097|work=Structurae|access-date=13 August 2010}}</ref> According to  plans, the tower was intended to reach a structural height of {{convert|360| m|feet|abbr=on}}.<ref name="web1" />

== History ==
The construction of the tower began at the end of 1983. In December 1986 the construction of the tower began on the prepared foundation. The barrel structures were completed at 220 metres on August 17, 1989. After the collapse of the USSR in 1991, construction work did not resume. In the early 1990s the facility was conserved. In 1993 the financing of the construction was closed. There were no investors to continue the construction.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Екатеринбургская телебашня. Досье - ТАСС |url=https://tass.ru/info/5060929 |access-date=2024-12-24 |website=TACC |language=ru}}</ref>

Until the year 2000 it was illegally used for [[buildering]] and [[BASE jumping]]. After several fatal accidents and suicides it was sealed.{{Citation needed|date=August 2010}}

On February 21, 2017, the regional Property Fund put up the TV tower and the adjacent land plot with an area of 46.8 thousand square meters for an electronic auction with an initial price of 652 million 772 thousand rubles. But the tower's privatization was canceled.<ref name=":0" />

The tower was demolished on 24 March 2018, as part of a city beautification programme in preparation for the [[2018 World Cup]].<ref name="BBC" /><ref>{{cite web|title=Снос телебашни в Екатеринбурге|url=https://ura.news/news/1052328328|work=ura.ru|date=24 March 2018 |access-date=24 March 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Russia blows up Soviet-era landmark in World Cup city|url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2018/03/russia-blows-soviet-era-landmark-world-cup-city-180324171705494.html|work=Al Jazeera|access-date=24 March 2018}}</ref>

The [[UMMC Arena]] was built on the site of the TV tower.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-03-24 |title=Необычные факты об исчезнувшей в Екатеринбурге телебашне |url=https://www.ural.kp.ru/daily/27255/4386637/ |access-date=2024-12-24 |website=www.ural.kp.ru/daily |language=ru}}</ref>
